passage: Naveen found the photo while looking for a charger cable: him and Suraj, sunburnt and grinning on the college trip to Goa, arms around each other. It had been two years since they last spoke properly. He sat on the edge of the bed in his Mumbai flat and typed once: "Found this today 🙂 Hope work is going well. Coffee if you're ever in town, no pressure at all." Suraj replied the next evening. "Haha, what a photo!! New job is crazy, but let's see soon." Naveen read it twice, felt a small pang, then a warm one. He put the photo back in the drawer and texted an old flatmate who lived nearby.

qa.a: The photo was taken on the college trip to Goa.

qa.q: How did Naveen feel after reading Suraj's reply?
qa.a: He felt a small pang first and then a warm feeling, fond of the memory while accepting that things had changed.

qa.q: What could Naveen do next to keep friendships healthy without pressing Suraj?
qa.a: Leave the door open with an occasional friendly message, and give time to friends who live nearby, as he already did. 🙂

qa.q: How might Suraj have seen Naveen's message?
qa.a: Suraj was probably touched but busy with a new job, so the vague reply may reflect a full schedule rather than a rejection.

grounding: Shows a young adult reaching out once to a drifting old friend without pressure and accepting the change with nostalgia.

passage:
"Pooja? It's Dhruv. From school."

"Dhruv! Oh my God. It's been, what, a year?"

"More. I saw your post about the baby. Congratulations."

"Thank you. She doesn't sleep. I haven't slept since March." Pooja laughed.

"I won't keep you long. I just... I miss our Sunday cricket and the chai after. I wanted to say hi."

"I miss it too. Honestly, I barely see anyone now. It's not you."

"I know." Dhruv paused. "I'm in Mumbai for a work thing in December. If you're free, coffee? And if you're not, that's completely fine."

"Let me see how the baby is. I'll message you?"

"Sure. No pressure at all."

After the call, Dhruv looked at the old photo on his fridge: the two of them, sixteen, holding a trophy. He smiled, a little sad. Some friendships change shape. That was okay.

qa.q: What did Dhruv and Pooja miss doing together?
qa.a: They missed Sunday cricket and the chai after.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling as he looked at the old photo after the call?
qa.a: Dhruv felt nostalgic and a little sad, but also accepting that the friendship had changed shape.

qa.q: What was good about how Dhruv reached out?
qa.a: Dhruv made one warm call, suggested a meeting without pressure, and accepted Pooja's limits.

qa.q: How does Pooja see the drift between them?
qa.a: Pooja feels it's because of Pooja's new life with the baby, not because of Dhruv, and she misses the old times too.

grounding: Shows a young adult reaching out once, without pressure, to a drifting friend and accepting the natural change in closeness.

passage:
Vinita and I shared a hostel room for three years. We knew each other's tea orders, exam panics and bad jokes. When she moved to Calgary, we promised to call every week.

For a while we did. Then it was every month. Now it's mostly hearts on each other's photos. I'm Aparna, and for a long time I was hurt about it, as if she'd chosen to leave me behind.

Last month, on her birthday, I sent one long voice note: that I missed her, that I hoped the snow wasn't too bad, and that she didn't need to reply at length.

She replied two days later, three sentences and a photo of her new dog. It stung for an evening.

Then I realised it wasn't nothing. She'd still thought of me. We're different people in different time zones. I kept the photo, made two cups of tea out of habit, and drank both.

qa.q: What was Aparna feeling when Vinita's reply came two days later?
qa.a: Aparna felt a sting of hurt and disappointment for an evening, then a gentler acceptance.

qa.q: Why was Aparna's single voice note a good way to reach out?
qa.a: It was warm and honest but put no pressure on Vinita to reply at length, leaving room for the friendship's new shape.

qa.q: How might Vinita see the change in their friendship?
qa.a: Vinita may still care but be busy with a new life, a new dog and a different time zone, so short replies may feel natural to her.

grounding: Shows a young adult reaching out once to a drifting friend without pressure and accepting the natural change in closeness.
